items.title: Live: Iran attacks US navy base after US retaliates over helicopter downing
items.description: Iran says it struck the US Navy's Fifth Fleet base in Bahrain with drones following a series of US strikes on Iranian cities along the Strait of Hormuz. Follow live.

items.title: Sea drone saves US helicopter crew downed in waters near Strait of Hormuz
items.description: A look at the US Corsair sea drone used in a first of its kind mission to rescue two helicopter crew shot down near the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Live: NSW and federal government tension over hospital bed backlog
items.description: NSW Health Minister Ryan Park airs frustrations over the issue of people stuck in hospital beds waiting for a spot in aged care or an NDIS placement. Follow live.

items.title: High Court decision could lead to tens of millions of dollars worth of immigration claims
items.description: There are warnings a High Court ruling allowing a man to sue for false imprisonment over his indefinite immigration detention will lead to more claims running into the tens of millions of dollars.

items.title: Woolworths to offshore hundreds of corporate jobs
items.description: Supermarket giant Woolworths will begin consultations with potentially affected staff today after announcing plans to shift some operations offshore.

items.title: 'When Neale spoke, people felt it': Daniher farewelled at MCG funeral
items.description: Family, friends, members of the AFL community and dignitaries are attending the service to remember the AFL legend, MND campaigner and former Australia of the Year.

items.title: Bishop alleges 'coercive threats', 'overreach' by university regulator in resignation letter
items.description: The former ANU chancellor has accused the university regulator of "grievously" constraining her ability to do her role in a withering resignation letter tabled in parliament.

items.title: Judge throws out appeals over homophobic tweet judgement
items.description: A Federal Court judge has dismissed an appeal against a judgement which ordered New South Wales MP Mark Latham to pay $140,000 to independent MP Alex Greenwich over a homophobic tweet in 2023.

items.title: Bear attack in Japan car park captured on CCTV as cities record more and more wild encounters
items.description: Bear encounters are rising in Japan, and the problem is not confined to the wilderness.

items.title: Military officers behind acid attack on Indonesian activist sentenced
items.description: Four military intelligence officers are sentenced to up to three years in jail, after they threw sulphuric acid over a human rights activist in a brazen attack in Central Jakarta.

items.title: Police release body-worn footage of fugitive bikie's dramatic arrest
items.description: Northern Territory Police have released dramatic body-worn footage of the arrest of Mongols bikie Brandt Graham after the 44-year-old jumped a court dock last week, sparking a five-day manhunt.

items.title: When does the FIFA World Cup start and who are the favourites?
items.description: The FIFA World Cup is the biggest single-sport event on the planet and has delivered numerous historical moments, from Diego Maradona's "hand of God" in 1986 to Zinedine Zidane's infamous headbutt on Marco Materazzi.

items.title: Nant whisky founder Keith Batt to enter months-long fraud trial
items.description: Tasmanian whisky distillery owner Keith Batt is charged with more than 700 criminal offences, ranging from fraud, to stealing, to dishonestly obtaining a financial advantage.

items.title: The proposed NDIS cuts advocates worry could put women at risk
items.description: Planned cuts to NDIS community participation budgets could leave participants in unsafe environments, including increasing their risk of domestic violence, advocates have warned.

items.title: Hayley's husband escalated control during her pregnancy. Her story is not uncommon
items.description: Pregnancy is a time of greater autonomy and self-awareness for women. Because domestic violence is about power and control, a pregnancy can challenge that for a person who is using abuse.

items.title: Finding and saving the world's biggest trees before they disappear
items.description: It took a decade for researchers to find the tallest tree in East Asia. Now they know where the 84.1-metre conifer is, but the future of its species and other tall trees is dire.

items.title: Calling all budding storytellers living with disability
items.description: If you are an emerging content maker or journalist with disability and have a story to tell, now is your chance to work with the ABC to tell it.

items.title: Why was Rolf Harris never tried for his crimes in Australia?
items.description: Rolf Harris's conviction for child sexual abuse was shocking to those who saw him as a lovable larrikin. But the people who were abused by him are refusing to stay silent about the impacts of his crimes.

items.title: Live: ASX flat as US launches strikes on Iran, Australian EV sales continue to surge
items.description: Supermarket giant Woolworths will begin consulting with segments of its 10,000 corporate workers today, with plans to offshore hundreds of roles to Asia. The Australian share market has begun its day relatively flat. Follow live.

items.title: 'A pile of crap': Premier's mea culpa over Ogilvie scandal
items.description: Tasmanian Premier Jeremy Rockliff says he "dropped the ball" regarding the allegations against a former minister, likening it to a "pile of crap" he has to clean up from "time to time".

items.title: Musk's xAI hit with class action over power plant's 'inescapable' noise
items.description: US residents say a plant powering data centres has caused them emotional distress and reduced the value of their properties.

items.title: How the relocation of a Bunnings store ignited a furore in this town
items.description: A plan by hardware giant Bunnings move its Bunbury store 10km to a neighbouring shire has angered and concerned residents and businesses.

items.title: Protests erupt in Belfast after stabbing attack, homes, cars and bus set on fire
items.description: Protesters hold anti-immigration demonstrations in Northern Ireland and England after a Sudanese man is arrested over a "brutal" knife attack in Belfast.

items.title: Why Xi's visit to North Korea is a flex for a new world order
items.description: Xi Jinping and Kim Jong Un's bilateral talks in North Korea were a big departure from the Chinese president's usual diplomacy playbook because, for this first time this year, he was the one travelling abroad to make the meeting happen.

items.title: Beekeepers call for access to new biopesticide to target varroa mite
items.description: A new biopesticide could help battle growing resistance to varroa mite treatments in Australia.
